In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DCCD inhibitory site in ECF1 is not located at the catalytic sites, but is located outside the substrate binding site.
DCCD reacts with the ECF1 beta subunits to produce a conformational change which inhibits the ATPase activity by blocking the cooperativity between the catalytic sites.
DCCD inhibits ECF1 activity by reacting with the beta subunits, thereby preventing the formation of a multisite complex and thus the cooperativity between the catalytic sites.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DCCD binding sites on ECF1 are located outside the catalytic sites and that DCCD inhibits ECF1 by preventing cooperativity between the catalytic sites.

the beta subunits of ECF1 are the sites of binding for DCCD, that this reagent does not bind in the active site for ATP, that it blocks cooperativity between catalytic sites, and that it inhibits unisite catalytic activity to a lesser extent.
DCCD is a very potent inhibitor of the multisite catalytic activity of the ECF1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the binding of DCCD to the ECF1 beta subunit does not inhibit the catalytic site of this subunit, but does block the cooperativity between the beta subunit and the alpha subunit catalytic sites.
the DCCD inhibition of unisite activity and steady-state activity is due to the same mechanism, i.e., the inhibition of cooperativity.
the inhibition of ECF1 by DCCD is a complex phenomenon and that the inhibition pattern is not consistent with a single site model.
